record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.original_question: After realistic detector-response simulations and background modeling, what final neutrino-nucleus interaction event rates would be obtained at a low-energy beta-beam facility for target nuclei such as deuteron, oxygen, iron, and lead, given that preliminary rates assume 100% efficiency and realistic ion intensities from feasibility studies?

evidence.quote: Note that the rates shown are obtained by considering realistic ion intensities, namely 2 × 1013 ¯ν/s (from 6He decay) and 8 × 1011 ν/s (from 18Ne decay), as obtained in the first feasibility study [34]. An efficiency of 100% is considered for all cases. Final rates will be given by detailed simulations of the detector response taking into account possible backgrounds.
Neutrino-nucleus interaction rates (events/year) at a low-energy beta-beam facility [38]: Rates on deuteron, oxygen, iron and lead are shown as examples.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hypothetical low-energy beta-beam neutrino facility in which intense beams of electron antineutrinos and electron neutrinos are produced by accelerating and storing radioactive ions whose beta decays yield neutrino fluxes. Assume the following baseline parameters from feasibility studies: an antineutrino production rate of 2 × 10^13 ν̄_e per second from the beta decay of ^6He and a neutrino production rate of 8 × 10^11 ν_e per second from the beta decay of ^18Ne, with the ions circulating in a storage ring of specified geometry that determines the neutrino flux at a downstream detector. Preliminary event-rate estimates for charged-current and neutral-current neutrino–nucleus interactions on the target nuclei deuteron (^2H), oxygen (^16O), iron (^56Fe), and lead (^208Pb) have been computed using theoretical inclusive cross sections and assuming 100% detection efficiency with no background.

Problem. Replace the idealized 100% efficiency / zero-background assumption with a realistic treatment of detector response — including energy thresholds, energy and angular resolutions, particle-identification efficiencies, fiducial acceptance, and the dominant beam-induced and ambient backgrounds — and determine the resulting annual event rates (events per year) for charged-current and neutral-current neutrino–nucleus interactions on each of the four target nuclei ^2H, ^16O, ^56Fe, and ^208Pb, while keeping the ion intensities and storage-ring parameters fixed at the feasibility-study values stated above.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature contains preliminary event-rate estimates at low-energy beta-beam facilities for nuclei including deuteron, oxygen, iron, and lead under idealized (100% efficiency, no background) assumptions, and various simulations of neutrino signals on specific detector materials have appeared. However, no comprehensive, definitive set of final event rates incorporating full realistic detector response and background modeling for all four targets is established, and the low-energy beta-beam facility itself remains a proposal rather than a constructed experiment. The status is therefore best classified as unknown/unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino-nucleus interaction rates at a low-energy β-beam facility
status_evidence.snippet: Computes expected neutrino detection rates at a low-energy β-beam facility for various nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Preliminary rates exist for several target nuclei under idealized assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Low energy neutrino scattering measurements at future facilities
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses low-energy neutrino measurement programs at future facilities including beta-beams.
status_evidence.claim: Final detector-realistic rates remain a topic of ongoing study.

status_evidence.title: Simulated Neutrino Signals of Low and Intermediate Energy Neutrinos on Cd Detectors
status_evidence.snippet: Simulations of β-beam neutrino signals on specific detector targets have been performed.
status_evidence.claim: Detector-specific simulations have been carried out for some nuclei but not a unified realistic study across deuteron, oxygen, iron, and lead.
